name: CloudWatch Guard
description: Protects native AWS CloudWatch observability: alarm deletion/silencing, dashboard removal, log-group subscription-filter removal (a common way to cut a log group off from a SIEM), and retention-policy changes. Complements AWS Extended, which only covers log-group/log-stream deletion. Monitoring Guard covers third-party tools (Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana, etc.), not native CloudWatch.

rules.name: Require access request for logs delete subscription filter
rules.description: aws logs delete-subscription-filter cuts a log group off from wherever it was streaming (SIEM, Lambda processor, Kinesis) — a common way to blind security monitoring without deleting the logs themselves.

rules.name: Require justification for cloudwatch delete alarms
rules.description: aws cloudwatch delete-alarms permanently removes one or more alarms (including composite alarms) and their history.

rules.name: Require justification for cloudwatch disable alarm actions
rules.description: aws cloudwatch disable-alarm-actions silences an alarm's notifications without deleting it — the alarm still shows as configured, making the silence easy to miss.

rules.name: Require justification for logs put retention policy
rules.description: aws logs put-retention-policy changes how long a log group is kept. Shortening it destroys older audit/forensic data on the next retention sweep.

rules.name: Warn on cloudwatch delete dashboards
rules.description: aws cloudwatch delete-dashboards removes one or more saved dashboards.

rules.name: Warn on logs delete metric filter
rules.description: aws logs delete-metric-filter removes a metric filter, breaking any alarm derived from it.

rules.name: Warn on cloudwatch set alarm state
rules.description: aws cloudwatch set-alarm-state manually overrides an alarm's state (e.g. forcing it to OK), which can mask an active incident until the next real evaluation.
